subject: System Design
title: The Saga Pattern
description: A quick, practical guide to The Saga Pattern.

hook.text: An order needs payment, inventory, and shipping. If payment succeeds but inventory fails, how do you roll back?

buildup.text: A saga is a sequence of local transactions. Each service executes its step and triggers the next.

discovery.text: If a step fails, compensating transactions undo previous steps: refund the payment, restore the inventory.

twist.text: Compensating transactions are tricky. You can't un-send an email. Some actions have no perfect undo.

climax.text: Sagas replace distributed transactions in microservices. They're complex but necessary for multi-service workflows.

punchline.text: Chain local transactions with compensating undo steps.

quiz.question: What is a compensating transaction in a saga?
options: An action that undoes a previous step when a later step fails
A faster version of the original transaction
